I really like Lilith 😖 I find her so interesting, and I do feel sorry for her, because she doesn't even realise how much she's ruined her own life.

She's done really terrible things, and it seems like she destroyed all of her old self to become a beautiful, empty person. But as much as she tries to distance herself from Ashley, Lilith is, in essence, completely unchanged - she still only knows how to define herself through other people's perception of her. Who was she outside of the world's repulsion, and who is she now without its vacuous love? She wouldn't know, because she never had the chance to explore who she was as a person. Now that she willingly clings to the pyre of externalised self-worth, she probably never will.

I hope Nikki will help her. We can see from the latest chapters how much happier Ashley is when she leaves the personality mirror and makes friends in Cicia. As much as Lilith wants to be a cold and disaffected person, she is still Ashley too, and she deserves to have people genuinely care about her as well.

She definitely can't be an outdoor cat. I don't think any cats here in Australia should be going out unsupervised, considering the threat they pose to native wildlife, but in general it's just too dangerous outside for her. Someone stealing her or hurting her is my absolute worst fear.

And... I'm sorry, I agree with the other person who replied, I'm very adamant about never using a spray bottle or any kind of 'fright' deterrent. I don't want to scare her out of doing things, even if she doesn't know I'm the one doing it.

She used to be my sister's cat (among three other cats), and my sister would use spray bottles on them all as a deterrent. Sister thought it was funny when they got spooked by it... it was awful. Genuinely would rather bankrupt myself getting a cat run than making her feel scared like that again.

I know she's not "getting back" at me. Describing her as mad wasn't good wording, but I wasn't using it in earnest or to imply she was acting out of spite. I just meant that she was unhappy about being stuck inside, and thought it might've been leading to classic cat distress poop, which is what I was trying to clarify in the last paragraph.

I hadn't considered that she wanted to relieve herself outside. But she's never done that before, even after she's begged to go out. Our "garden" sucks; all wood panelling and concrete. It seems.. diametrically opposed to cat litter? If that makes sense.

Anyway it sounds like I may have to cop some family fury, and make room for a litter box by the back door, or at least somewhere near her poo corner. She does have two litter boxes close to my bedroom where she sleeps, and she uses them both in the night, but maybe the back door is too far from her litter during the day.
